summary: Cloud scan of https://juice-shop.herokuapp.com complete. Found 0 critical and 2 high vulnerabilities.

findings.name: Missing Permissions-Policy Header
findings.description: The 'Permissions-Policy' header is not set. This header allows a website to control browser features (e.g., camera, microphone, geolocation) available to itself and to any embedded iframes. Without it, the site might be vulnerable to feature abuse by third-party content or cross-origin attacks, allowing potentially malicious scripts to access sensitive user features or data.

technical_evidence.response_headers_excerpt: Permissions-Policy header not found in the HTTP response.

findings.recommendation: Implement the 'Permissions-Policy' header to control browser features. Define a policy that restricts access to sensitive features to only those explicitly required by the application. For example: `Permissions-Policy: geolocation=(), camera=(), microphone=()` to disable these features for the origin and any embedded content, or `Permissions-Policy: geolocation=(self)` to allow only the origin to use geolocation.

findings.name: Server Header Disclosure (X-Powered-By)
findings.description: The 'X-Powered-By' header is disclosed in the HTTP response, revealing the underlying technology (Express framework). This information can be used by attackers to identify known vulnerabilities associated with specific software versions or configurations, potentially aiding in targeted attacks.
findings.recommendation: Remove or obscure the 'X-Powered-By' header to prevent the disclosure of server-side technologies. This typically involves configuring the web server or application framework (e.g., Express) to suppress this header. For Express, this can be done by setting `app.disable('x-powered-by');`.

findings.name: Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA) / Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR)
findings.description: The application is vulnerable to Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA), also known as Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR). An authenticated user can access and retrieve sensitive information belonging to other users by manipulating the `id` parameter in the API endpoint `/api/Users/{id}`. This bypasses intended authorization controls, allowing unauthorized access to user profiles.

requests_responses.description: Request made by an authorized user (e.g., User ID 1) to retrieve their own profile.
Request made by the same authorized user (User ID 1) to retrieve another user's profile (User ID 2) by changing the 'id' parameter.

technical_evidence.comparison_proof: Comparison of the responses clearly shows that User ID 1 was able to successfully retrieve the profile details (including email and other data) of User ID 2 by simply incrementing the `id` parameter. Both responses returned a 200 OK status, confirming successful unauthorized access to a different user's resource.

findings.recommendation: Implement robust object-level authorization checks for all API endpoints that handle user-specific or sensitive data. Ensure that the server validates if the authenticated user has the necessary permissions to access the requested object ID before returning any data. This typically involves comparing the `id` in the request path with the authenticated user's own ID or checking against a role-based access control (RBAC) system.
